issues.title: fix(chatgptauth): name the failing check in ID-token verification errors
issues.body:
## Description

Fixes #1942, motivated by #1938.

`verifyAt` validated nine distinct ID-token conditions — issuer, subject, audience, expiry, issued-at, not-before, authorized party, multi-audience/azp — and returned the same combined error (`ID-token issuer, audience, subject or lifetime did not match`) for all of them. A rejected login gave no hint about which condition actually failed, which makes reports like #1938 impossible to triage without a debugger.

The checks are now split into a switch returning a specific message per condition, and the 5-second issued-at/not-before clock tolerance is a named constant (`idTokenClockSkew`) instead of two magic literals. No validation behavior changes — only the error text, plus the named constant.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] `make test` passes locally
- [x] Manual testing (describe below)

`TestVerifyIDToken` now asserts, for every tampered-claim case, that the returned error names the failing check (e.g. tampering `iat` to an hour ahead must produce `ID-token issued-at is in the future`). The new assertion fails on main's combined message and passes with this change; the full suite and `make check` are green.

issues.title: fix(tool): normalize cancelled git exit status 1 on Windows with nil Runner
issues.body:
## Description

On Windows, cancelling or timing out `exec.CommandContext` terminates the child `git` process via `TerminateProcess`. The child process exits with code 1 instead of a Unix signal.

Before this fix, Windows hit two bugs on cancellation.

First, callers that passed a `nil` `*gitcmd.Runner` skipped `gitcmd.Runner` and called `exec.CommandContext` directly. Those callers returned raw `exit status 1` and leaked partial output instead of `context.Canceled` or `context.DeadlineExceeded`.

Second, `ResolveWorkspaceComparison` checked `show-ref` exit code 1 for an unborn branch before checking `ctx.Err()`. On Windows, a killed `show-ref` process also exits with code 1.

This PR routes all git subprocess calls through `gitcmd.Runner` and checks `ctx.Err()` first.

- Make `nil` `*gitcmd.Runner` run git commands directly with no concurrency limit.
- Normalize non-zero exits under a cancelled or expired context to `ctx.Err()` in `Run`, `Output`, `RunSplit`, and `Stream`.
- Check `ctx.Err()` before treating `show-ref` exit code 1 as an unborn branch in `internal/diff/workspace.go`.
- Delete duplicate `else` branches that called `exec.CommandContext` in `internal/diff`, `internal/tool`, `internal/scan`, and `internal/config/rules`.
- Add cross-platform git shim tests in `internal/gitcmd`, `internal/diff`, `internal/tool`, and `internal/scan`. They verify cancellation across pooled and `nil` runners.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] CI / Build / Tooling

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] `make test` passes locally
- [x] Manual testing (describe below)

Ran locally on Windows with Git Bash and MSYS2 make ahead of System32 in `PATH`.

- `make check` passed across license headers, 863 source files for English-only text, `go mod tidy`, `gofmt -s -w .`, and `go vet`.
- `make build` built `opencodereview.exe` with no errors.
- `make test` ran `LC_ALL=C go test -v -race -count=1` across all 26 non-extension packages and passed.
- `make coverage` passed with 91.3% statement coverage, above the 90% minimum.

issues.title: bug(tool): context cancellation with nil Runner returns exit status 1 on Windows
issues.body:
### OpenCodeReview Version

v1.13.10

### Operating System

Windows

### Installation Method

Built from source

### LLM Provider

Other OpenAI-compatible endpoint

### Bug Description

When `git` is run without a `gitcmd.Runner` (`Runner == nil`) and the `context` gets cancelled, both `Provider.runGitSplit` (`internal/diff/git.go`) and `CodeSearchProvider.runGitGrep` (`internal/tool/code_search.go`) only return `ctx.Err()` if the process exit code is `-1`.

That works on Unix (`SIGKILL` gives `-1`), but on Windows `exec.CommandContext` kills the process with exit code `1`. So on Windows with `Runner == nil`:
- `internal/diff` returns a generic `exit status 1` error instead of `context.Canceled` / `context.DeadlineExceeded`.
- `CodeSearchProvider.gitGrep` can hit `exitCode == 1` on a timeout (when stdout/stderr are empty) and return `"No matches found"` instead of an error.

Note that the existing `Runner != nil` path already returns `ctx.Err()` regardless of exit code, and normal CLI commands pass a real `Runner`. Right now this affects `nil`-runner callers and Windows tests—`TestGetDiff_CancelledMidWriteReportsCancellation` (`internal/diff/git_error_test.go`) actually passes `nil`, so it would catch this, except `shimGit` skips on Windows because it uses `#!/bin/sh`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. On Windows, run the cancellation test:
   ```powershell
   go test -v -run TestGetDiff_CancelledMidWriteReportsCancellation ./internal/diff
   ```
   It skips immediately instead of testing Windows cancellation.

2. Check what `exec.CommandContext` returns on Windows when a timeout kills a child process:
   ```go
   ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 50*time.Millisecond)
   defer cancel()
   cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "ping", "-n", "10", "127.0.0.1")
   err := cmd.Run()
   fmt.Printf("ctx.Err=%v err=%v exitCode=%d\n", ctx.Err(), err, cmd.ProcessState.ExitCode())
   // Output: ctx.Err=context deadline exceeded err=exit status 1 exitCode=1
   ```

### Expected Behavior

- With `Runner == nil`, cancellation on Windows should return `ctx.Err()` just like it does on Unix and when `Runner != nil`.
- `TestGetDiff_CancelledMidWriteReportsCancellation` should run on Windows (for example, using a small Go helper instead of a `#!/bin/sh` script) instead of skipping.

### Logs / Error Output

```shell
=== RUN   TestGetDiff_CancelledMidWriteReportsCancellation
    git_error_test.go:208: PATH shim relies on a shebang script
--- SKIP: TestGetDiff_CancelledMidWriteReportsCancellation (0.00s)
```

### AI/LLM Disclosure

- [ ] I didn't use AI/LLM to assist or generate the content above.

### Additional Context

AI disclosure: I found this while reading internal/diff; Antigravity helped double-check callers on main and write up this report.

issues.title: fix(llmloop): handle visible findings text alongside task_done
issues.body:
## Description

### Root Cause
In `internal/llmloop/loop.go` (`runMainTask`), when a model response included tool calls and one of them completed the task (`Action == Complete`, i.e., `task_done`), the loop returned `true, StopNone, nil` immediately without checking whether any findings had actually been recorded in the subtask or whether the response carried non-empty visible prose.

As a result, when a model wrote its review findings as visible text alongside `task_done` without calling `code_comment`, those findings were silently dropped and the subtask finished with `status: complete`, 0 findings, and no warning. Because `internal/reviewtask` backs both `ocr review` and `ocr scan`, both modes were affected.

### Changes
- Added generic, opt-in completion validation fields on `llmloop.Task` (`UnfiledCompletionMessage`, `UnfiledCompletionWarning`) and `llmloop.ToolOutcome` (`RecordedSubmission`) in `internal/llmloop/task.go` so `llmloop` remains decoupled from review-specific tool names.
- Updated `Runner.runMainTask` (`internal/llmloop/loop.go`) to track `hasSubmission` and `nudgedUnfiledCompletion` per conversation invocation:
  - When a task completes via `Action == Complete` with non-empty visible text and `!hasSubmission`:
    - If `UnfiledCompletionMessage` is configured and no nudge has been sent yet (and another round or grace round remains), append the turn and prompt the model once to submit any findings via `code_comment` or re-confirm `task_done` without findings text.
    - If the model subsequently files findings (`RecordedSubmission: true`) or re-confirms completion cleanly without unfiled text, finish normally with no warning.
    - If it still completes with unfiled visible text after the bounded nudge (or during `runGraceRound`), record the configured `UnfiledCompletionWarning` so callers and reports never mistake dropped findings text for a clean zero-finding review.
- Configured `internal/reviewtask/task.go` to mark successful `code_comment` invocations (`checkpoint.Data == tool.CommentSucceed`) as `RecordedSubmission: true`, set `UnfiledCompletionMessage`, and define `WarningTaskDoneWithUnfiledText = "task_done_with_unfiled_text"`.
- Added regression tests in `internal/reviewtask/loop_test.go` (`TestRunMainTask_ProseWithTaskDone`) and `internal/llmloop/task_test.go` (`TestTaskUnfiledCompletionNudgeAndWarning`).

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

issues.title: fix(llm): send session affinity headers for ChatGPT plan cache routing
issues.body:
## Description

### Root Cause
In `OpenAIResponsesClient.CompletionsWithCtx` (`internal/llm/responses_client.go`), requests already carry a per-task session key in context (`SessionKeyFromContext`) and `req.SessionID` as `prompt_cache_key` in the request body. However, when `ChatGPTPlan` is enabled (`provider: chatgpt`), no HTTP session affinity routing headers (`session_id` / `session-id`) were attached unless manually configured via `extra_headers`.

Because the ChatGPT backend routes prompt-cache state using session routing headers for sticky worker affinity, consecutive turns in a review loop could land on different backend shards and miss the warm KV prefix cache despite an append-only history. Additionally, ChatGPT callers that tag only context with `ContextWithSessionKey` (without populating `req.SessionID`, such as plan/grouping/compression turns) left `prompt_cache_key` unset.

### Changes
- Added `chatGPTSessionAffinityKey(ctx, reqSessionID, fallbackKey)` in `internal/llm/responses_client.go` with precedence: `SessionKeyFromContext(ctx)` -> `req.SessionID` -> client `SessionKey` fallback.
- When `c.cfg.ChatGPTPlan` is enabled:
  - Attach `session_id` and `session-id` HTTP headers using the resolved affinity key before applying `c.cfg.ExtraHeaders` (so explicit `extra_headers` overrides with `{ocr_session_key}` expansion continue to take precedence).
  - Default `params.PromptCacheKey` to the resolved affinity key when `req.SessionID` is empty (without overriding explicit `req.SessionID` or `extra_body.prompt_cache_key`).
- Left non-`ChatGPTPlan` Responses clients completely unchanged.
- Added HTTP roundtrip tests in `internal/llm/chatgpt_roundtrip_test.go` (`TestChatGPTPromptCacheAffinityHeaders`).
